messages.author: d855414f42bdeb3f
messages.subject: Utilizing earth package with qplot/ggplot?
parts:
I am new to ggplot and working through building up the various aspects/layers of the plots.  It is easy to overlay a linear regression line over a scatter plot but I am curious  (and apologies if this has been discussed) if there is a way to overlay a regression spline using the earth package onto a scatterplot, essentially getting a regression spline overlayed.  Thoughts?

Jason

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Utilizing earth package with qplot/ggplot?
parts:
If you're talking about a pseudo-3D plot, then no. If the graph is 2D,
one option is to extract the x, y and predicted values from the object
returned by earth(), put them into a data frame, call it with ggplot()
and use geom_line() or geom_path(). Alternatively, you could use
geom_smooth() and define a formula of the form y ~ f(x) for some
function f of one variable that is accessible by ggplot2 (and the
formula has to have 'y' on the left and be a function of 'x', not the
variables in your data). If you post a small, reproducible example,
maybe someone here could provide more specific help.

Dennis

parts:
The graph is 2d, the component I am looking to utilize is essentially like a linear regression line except that it is a set of splines from the earth package.

I have attached a sample data file as well as a sample R script that loads the data, performs a necessary conversion and then runs the earth spline against it.  I have two plots, one is the scatter plot of the data, the other is the regression spline produced by the earth package.  I am looking to overlay the regression spline atop the scatterplot.  Not sure how to extract the X,Y, predict values from the model.  Any help would be appreciated, thanks!

Jason
